The lap-1 e2e test 'cap-unknown refusal: relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' now sees 3 calls instead of 2. My `force: overCap` change! The flow: 'go' (headless) → the refusal (call 1) → the heal: relief `_runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]')` — no force → the funnel no-ops (tiny transcript) → coalesce retry (call 2) → 'ok'. NOW: 3 calls. What's the third? `_runPrompt`'s PRE-FLIGHT `_maybeAutoCompact` — before the refusal there's no pending pass... The 3rd call must be AFTER: the turn's POST-RUN... the turn ended with the coalesce answer; at `_afterRun`: `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: no learned cap (cap-unknown), pending pass... — WAS the pass armed by the refusal AND consumed by the relief's gate? The relief path doesn't consult the gate (no gate call — earlier trace showed the consumption at `_afterRun`). NOW with `force: overCap`: at `_afterRun`, `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: `takePremptivePass` TRUE (armed by the refusal, never consumed — the relief doesn't consume it) → overCap=true → funnel **force: true** → the funnel COMPACTS (chunk call #3!) on the tiny transcript → the report '[auto-compacted]'...

So my force change made the E1 pass fire a (pointless) compaction on the tiny transcript at the post-run point. The e2e test pins calls==2.

Hmm — is the extra pass HARMFUL? It compacted a tiny transcript (nothing hideable — the funnel's cut... it DID issue a chunk call — so it summarized something — 'ok' turn hidden?). For a cap-unknown model, the pass firing on the next request is EXACTLY the E1 design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way") — the post-run compaction IS a legitimate firing point ("the next request" = before the NEXT request — post-run is before the next request ✓). But it costs a summarizer call on a transcript that's ALREADY tiny (the relief no-op'd for the same reason).

The DESIGN question: should the pass fire when the transcript has NOTHING to compact? The relief said no-op; the funnel forced a pass anyway → it found "something" to summarize (a 2-message transcript!?) — wait, it can't hide 2 messages (keep region) — the chunk call happened though (3 calls total = refusal + retry + 1 chunk) — so the funnel DID call the summarizer on the tiny transcript — a WASTED call. The classic engine: `force: true` → runs a pass regardless → the cut found the first message hideable? ('go' + partial?) — whatever: it burns a call.

The e2e's contract ('relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' → calls==2) is the SHIPPED behavior the reviewer didn't contest. My force change altered it. Options:

(a) Force only when the trigger is the PENDING PASS, not the count trigger:
```dart
final passWasPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(...);
final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
...
await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: passWasPending);
``
Same behavior in the E1-switch test (its trigger WAS the pending pass). But at the post-run point in the e2e: passWasPending true → force → STILL the extra chunk call! Same outcome.

(b) Make the FUNEL smarter: when forced AND the transcript has nothing hideable → skip without a summarizer call. That's engine-level surgery — beyond scope.

(c) Don't force at all; instead RE-ARM the pass in the defer branch (the reviewer's alternative: "or call _modelCaps to re-arm before the early return"). Re-arm = the pass survives the boot AND fires later... but the SAME silent-no-op problem at the pre-flight: the gate consumes at the pre-flight, the funnel no-ops (learnedCap null) → the pass is gone with no compaction — the original bug remains (my whole force change exists to fix that).

(d) Force ONLY at the PRE-FLIGHT site when the trigger was the pending pass (not at _afterRun/post-run/relief): the pre-flight is where the reviewer's contract lives ("the cap still lands BEFORE any user work"). The e2e's extra call came from the POST-RUN (`_afterRun`) — with (d) it stays a no-op → calls==2 ✓. My E1-switch test: the pass fires at the PRE-FLIGHT (forced) ✓.

How: `_maybeAutoCompact` gets a `forcePass: bool = false` param — the PRE-FLIGHT caller passes true; `_afterRun` and the over-window funnel call it default-false. Hmm — but `_maybeAutoCompact` computes overCap internally... Let me re-shape:

```dart
Future<bool> _maybeAutoCompact({bool forceE1Pass = false}) async {
 ...
 final passPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(model.provider, model.id);
 final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
 ...
 await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: forceE1Pass && passPending);
``
And `_beginUserPrompt` calls `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)` (the pre-flight = before user work). `_afterRun` (line 278) calls plain. Line 1001 (over-window continuation) plain.

Wait — but with forceE1Pass=false at the post-run, the pass gets CONSUMED by the gate (overCap=true) and the funnel no-ops → the pass silently dropped at post-run — the SAME bug class at a different site! For the post-run: the transcript just grew by the turn; the next turn's pre-flight would... the pass is gone. Hmm. But consuming-then-nop at post-run was the PRE-EXISTING behavior (the reviewer's finding was about the BOOT only). Not expanding scope: the reviewer's scenario is the boot-consume. Keep post-run as-is.

Hmm — actually wait: is forceE1Pass=true at the PRE-FLIGHT even necessary for correctness beyond my E1 test? The reviewer's contract: "the cap still lands BEFORE any user work continues". With peek-at-boot + consuming-gate-at-preflight + force → the pre-flight compacts ✓. With forceE1Pass=false the pre-flight consumes + no-ops (silent drop) → the request rides out → the bug. So YES, needed at the pre-flight.

So: `_beginUserPrompt` → `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`; others unchanged. The E1-switch test stays green (pre-flight forced). The e2e returns to calls==2 (the post-run gate consumes without forcing — the shipped no-op).

The E1 pass's POINT is compaction before the request; on a tiny transcript there's nothing to compact — the wasted call is unfortunate but the pass is one-shot by design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way" — for a transcript THAT small the refusal wouldn't recur...). The alternative (no force) = the silent drop. The forced pass at least gives the funnel the chance to coalesce/cut. The reviewer's fix intent wins; the wasted-call edge on tiny transcripts is acceptable (and un-tested territory). ## Thread: the deferred boot consumes the armed E1 one-shot pass (IMPORTANT)

**Fixed** — two changes, TDD'd (RED reproduced, then GREEN):

1. **The boot-cap decision now PEEKS the armed pass instead of consuming it.** `_capResumedContext` uses a new non-consuming gate `_messageCapGatePending()` (`isPremptivePassPending`) for its decision; the consuming `_messageCapGateReached()` stays only on paths that actually run a compaction when it returns true. A pending pass is now spent only where a compaction runs.

2. **The pass now ACTS at the first turn's pre-flight.** Testing the peek fix exposed a second half of the same hole: `_maybeAutoCompact`'s gate consumed the pass and handed `force: false` to the compactor, whose own re-check cannot see a cap-UNKNOWN model's pass (no learned cap to trip `_overMessageCap`) — so the funnel silently no-oped and the pass was still dropped. The pre-flight (`_beginUserPrompt` → `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`) now forces the funnel when the armed pass is its trigger. The post-run fold keeps its shipped no-op-when-under-trigger behavior (`forceE1Pass` defaults false), so the cap-unknown heal e2e (`relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry`, `calls == 2`) is unchanged.

**Test** (`test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart`, "E1 pass (gh-1729 review)"): a cap-unknown refusal arms the pass mid-REPL (the heal's retry is interrupted — the abort skips the post-run fold, so the pass is still pending), a `/session` switch to a 40-kept-message session (~40k tokens, under the token trigger — the armed pass is the ONLY trigger) defers with the visible note and zero LM calls, and the first turn's pre-flight then compacts BEFORE the request: the turn context rides the compacted 22-message transcript, `auto-compacted` rendered. Verified RED against the old consuming gate and GREEN with the fix.

## Thread: the mid-REPL switch regime has zero automated coverage / stale-abort protection gone (IMPORTANT)

**Fixed** — the skip is gone; the regime runs un-skipped:

1. **Race-free switch coverage (un-skipped).** The `AC3 lazy switch` test no longer rides `skip:`. The #1728 wedge shape this suite could hit ("the input pump processes the queued prompt while the switch's async tail is still in flight") is closed by waiting for the switch's **terminal** line — `switched to session '…'`, printed in `_switchToMetadata` after every awaited step (usage-ledger flush, context reload, session load, the boot cap, lease re-claim, viewer banner, subagent rehydrate) — before any prompt is sent. The test then asserts: the switch settles with **zero LM calls**, the deferred-regime note renders, and the first turn's pre-flight compacts before the request (`auto-compacted`, request ≤ trigger). Verified stable across repeated runs. The comment names #1728: if the machinery-side wedge (a switch that never completes at all) ever recurs, the wait now turns it into a loud timeout instead of a silently-wedged pass.

2. **Stale-abort interaction is covered again** — at the level where the flag actually matters, inside the new `E1 pass (gh-1729 review)` test: the first turn's heal-retry is hung and **interrupted** (`_runAbortRequested` set, the abort skips the post-run fold), then the switch clears the flag (`_switchToMetadata`) — proven by the deferred-regime note rendering at the boot gate (it would be suppressed otherwise) — and `_beginUserPrompt` clears it again so the first turn's pre-flight fires. Both halves of the flag lifecycle are asserted; no PTY/lease machinery involved.

3. The skip's own disclosure points are moot (no skip remains); the skip-reason-naming-ticket ask no longer applies. The lazy-boot contract assertions the old skipped test carried (zero LM calls at the switch, pre-flight compacts before the request) are all preserved in the un-skipped test.

## Thread: log the deferred regime visibly at boot (SUGGESTION)

**Fixed** — adopted verbatim. The defer branch in `_capResumedContext` now emits the dim note after its diagnostic line:

```dart
io.writeln(
  _style.dim(
    '[resume] context over the compaction trigger (~$tokens tokens, '
    'inside the window) — compaction deferred to the first message',
  ),
);
```

It is asserted in all three lazy-regime tests (`AC5` direct resume, the un-skipped `AC3 lazy switch`, and the `E1 pass` test), so the note is regression-pinned on both the boot and the switch paths. Side benefit noted in the E1 test: for a transcript under the token trigger, the note is also the observable proof the armed E1 pass made the boot gate true (it only prints when `overCap` is true).

blocks.text:
The lap-1 e2e test 'cap-unknown refusal: relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' now sees 3 calls instead of 2. My `force: overCap` change! The flow: 'go' (headless) → the refusal (call 1) → the heal: relief `_runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]')` — no force → the funnel no-ops (tiny transcript) → coalesce retry (call 2) → 'ok'. NOW: 3 calls. What's the third? `_runPrompt`'s PRE-FLIGHT `_maybeAutoCompact` — before the refusal there's no pending pass... The 3rd call must be AFTER: the turn's POST-RUN... the turn ended with the coalesce answer; at `_afterRun`: `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: no learned cap (cap-unknown), pending pass... — WAS the pass armed by the refusal AND consumed by the relief's gate? The relief path doesn't consult the gate (no gate call — earlier trace showed the consumption at `_afterRun`). NOW with `force: overCap`: at `_afterRun`, `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: `takePremptivePass` TRUE (armed by the refusal, never consumed — the relief doesn't consume it) → overCap=true → funnel **force: true** → the funnel COMPACTS (chunk call #3!) on the tiny transcript → the report '[auto-compacted]'...

So my force change made the E1 pass fire a (pointless) compaction on the tiny transcript at the post-run point. The e2e test pins calls==2.

Hmm — is the extra pass HARMFUL? It compacted a tiny transcript (nothing hideable — the funnel's cut... it DID issue a chunk call — so it summarized something — 'ok' turn hidden?). For a cap-unknown model, the pass firing on the next request is EXACTLY the E1 design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way") — the post-run compaction IS a legitimate firing point ("the next request" = before the NEXT request — post-run is before the next request ✓). But it costs a summarizer call on a transcript that's ALREADY tiny (the relief no-op'd for the same reason).

The DESIGN question: should the pass fire when the transcript has NOTHING to compact? The relief said no-op; the funnel forced a pass anyway → it found "something" to summarize (a 2-message transcript!?) — wait, it can't hide 2 messages (keep region) — the chunk call happened though (3 calls total = refusal + retry + 1 chunk) — so the funnel DID call the summarizer on the tiny transcript — a WASTED call. The classic engine: `force: true` → runs a pass regardless → the cut found the first message hideable? ('go' + partial?) — whatever: it burns a call.

The e2e's contract ('relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' → calls==2) is the SHIPPED behavior the reviewer didn't contest. My force change altered it. Options:

(a) Force only when the trigger is the PENDING PASS, not the count trigger:
```dart
final passWasPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(...);
final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
...
await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: passWasPending);
``
Same behavior in the E1-switch test (its trigger WAS the pending pass). But at the post-run point in the e2e: passWasPending true → force → STILL the extra chunk call! Same outcome.

(b) Make the FUNEL smarter: when forced AND the transcript has nothing hideable → skip without a summarizer call. That's engine-level surgery — beyond scope.

(c) Don't force at all; instead RE-ARM the pass in the defer branch (the reviewer's alternative: "or call _modelCaps to re-arm before the early return"). Re-arm = the pass survives the boot AND fires later... but the SAME silent-no-op problem at the pre-flight: the gate consumes at the pre-flight, the funnel no-ops (learnedCap null) → the pass is gone with no compaction — the original bug remains (my whole force change exists to fix that).

(d) Force ONLY at the PRE-FLIGHT site when the trigger was the pending pass (not at _afterRun/post-run/relief): the pre-flight is where the reviewer's contract lives ("the cap still lands BEFORE any user work"). The e2e's extra call came from the POST-RUN (`_afterRun`) — with (d) it stays a no-op → calls==2 ✓. My E1-switch test: the pass fires at the PRE-FLIGHT (forced) ✓.

How: `_maybeAutoCompact` gets a `forcePass: bool = false` param — the PRE-FLIGHT caller passes true; `_afterRun` and the over-window funnel call it default-false. Hmm — but `_maybeAutoCompact` computes overCap internally... Let me re-shape:

```dart
Future<bool> _maybeAutoCompact({bool forceE1Pass = false}) async {
 ...
 final passPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(model.provider, model.id);
 final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
 ...
 await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: forceE1Pass && passPending);
``
And `_beginUserPrompt` calls `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)` (the pre-flight = before user work). `_afterRun` (line 278) calls plain. Line 1001 (over-window continuation) plain.

Wait — but with forceE1Pass=false at the post-run, the pass gets CONSUMED by the gate (overCap=true) and the funnel no-ops → the pass silently dropped at post-run — the SAME bug class at a different site! For the post-run: the transcript just grew by the turn; the next turn's pre-flight would... the pass is gone. Hmm. But consuming-then-nop at post-run was the PRE-EXISTING behavior (the reviewer's finding was about the BOOT only). Not expanding scope: the reviewer's scenario is the boot-consume. Keep post-run as-is.

Hmm — actually wait: is forceE1Pass=true at the PRE-FLIGHT even necessary for correctness beyond my E1 test? The reviewer's contract: "the cap still lands BEFORE any user work continues". With peek-at-boot + consuming-gate-at-preflight + force → the pre-flight compacts ✓. With forceE1Pass=false the pre-flight consumes + no-ops (silent drop) → the request rides out → the bug. So YES, needed at the pre-flight.

So: `_beginUserPrompt` → `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`; others unchanged. The E1-switch test stays green (pre-flight forced). The e2e returns to calls==2 (the post-run gate consumes without forcing — the shipped no-op).

Hmm — one more corner: the pre-flight force fires a chunk call on a TINY transcript when a pass is pending (e.g., refusal in session A, then a prompt in session A on a tiny transcript — the E1 pass → forced pass → wasted chunk call!). The E1 pass's POINT is compaction before the request; on a tiny transcript there's nothing to compact — the wasted call is unfortunate but the pass is one-shot by design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way" — for a transcript THAT small the refusal wouldn't recur...). The alternative (no force) = the silent drop. The forced pass at least gives the funnel the chance to coalesce/cut. The reviewer's fix intent wins; the wasted-call edge on tiny transcripts is acceptable (and un-tested territory). 1. **E1 pass consumed at the deferred boot (IMPORTANT)** — wrote `E1 pass (gh-1729 review)` in `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart`: a cap-UNKNOWN refusal arms the pass mid-REPL (the heal's retry interrupted — the abort skips the post-run fold, leaving the pass pending), then a `/session` switch to a 40-kept session (~40k tokens, **under** the token trigger so the armed pass is the only compaction trigger) defers at boot, and the first turn's pre-flight must compact BEFORE the request. 2. **Switch-regime coverage (IMPORTANT)** — un-skipped the `AC3 lazy switch` test. The #1728 wedge shape (the input pump dispatching a queued prompt into the switch's async tail) is closed deterministically by waiting for the switch's **terminal** line (`switched to session '…'`, printed after every awaited `_switchToMetadata` step) before prompting. 3. **Deferred-regime note (SUGGESTION)** — adopted verbatim: the defer branch emits the dim `[resume] context over the compaction trigger (~N tokens, inside the window) — compaction deferred to the first message` note; asserted in all three lazy-regime tests (AC5 boot, lazy switch, E1 switch).

blocks.text:
The lap-1 e2e test 'cap-unknown refusal: relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' now sees 3 calls instead of 2. My `force: overCap` change! The flow: 'go' (headless) → the refusal (call 1) → the heal: relief `_runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]')` — no force → the funnel no-ops (tiny transcript) → coalesce retry (call 2) → 'ok'. NOW: 3 calls. What's the third? `_runPrompt`'s PRE-FLIGHT `_maybeAutoCompact` — before the refusal there's no pending pass... The 3rd call must be AFTER: the turn's POST-RUN... the turn ended with the coalesce answer; at `_afterRun`: `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: no learned cap (cap-unknown), pending pass... — WAS the pass armed by the refusal AND consumed by the relief's gate? The relief path doesn't consult the gate (no gate call — earlier trace showed the consumption at `_afterRun`). NOW with `force: overCap`: at `_afterRun`, `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: `takePremptivePass` TRUE (armed by the refusal, never consumed — the relief doesn't consume it) → overCap=true → funnel **force: true** → the funnel COMPACTS (chunk call #3!) on the tiny transcript → the report '[auto-compacted]'...

So my force change made the E1 pass fire a (pointless) compaction on the tiny transcript at the post-run point. The e2e test pins calls==2.

Hmm — is the extra pass HARMFUL? It compacted a tiny transcript (nothing hideable — the funnel's cut... it DID issue a chunk call — so it summarized something — 'ok' turn hidden?). For a cap-unknown model, the pass firing on the next request is EXACTLY the E1 design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way") — the post-run compaction IS a legitimate firing point ("the next request" = before the NEXT request — post-run is before the next request ✓). But it costs a summarizer call on a transcript that's ALREADY tiny (the relief no-op'd for the same reason).

The DESIGN question: should the pass fire when the transcript has NOTHING to compact? The relief said no-op; the funnel forced a pass anyway → it found "something" to summarize (a 2-message transcript!?) — wait, it can't hide 2 messages (keep region) — the chunk call happened though (3 calls total = refusal + retry + 1 chunk) — so the funnel DID call the summarizer on the tiny transcript — a WASTED call. The classic engine: `force: true` → runs a pass regardless → the cut found the first message hideable? ('go' + partial?) — whatever: it burns a call.

The e2e's contract ('relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' → calls==2) is the SHIPPED behavior the reviewer didn't contest. My force change altered it. Options:

(a) Force only when the trigger is the PENDING PASS, not the count trigger:
```dart
final passWasPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(...);
final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
...
await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: passWasPending);
``
Same behavior in the E1-switch test (its trigger WAS the pending pass). But at the post-run point in the e2e: passWasPending true → force → STILL the extra chunk call! Same outcome.

(b) Make the FUNEL smarter: when forced AND the transcript has nothing hideable → skip without a summarizer call. That's engine-level surgery — beyond scope.

(c) Don't force at all; instead RE-ARM the pass in the defer branch (the reviewer's alternative: "or call _modelCaps to re-arm before the early return"). Re-arm = the pass survives the boot AND fires later... but the SAME silent-no-op problem at the pre-flight: the gate consumes at the pre-flight, the funnel no-ops (learnedCap null) → the pass is gone with no compaction — the original bug remains (my whole force change exists to fix that).

(d) Force ONLY at the PRE-FLIGHT site when the trigger was the pending pass (not at _afterRun/post-run/relief): the pre-flight is where the reviewer's contract lives ("the cap still lands BEFORE any user work"). The e2e's extra call came from the POST-RUN (`_afterRun`) — with (d) it stays a no-op → calls==2 ✓. My E1-switch test: the pass fires at the PRE-FLIGHT (forced) ✓.

How: `_maybeAutoCompact` gets a `forcePass: bool = false` param — the PRE-FLIGHT caller passes true; `_afterRun` and the over-window funnel call it default-false. Hmm — but `_maybeAutoCompact` computes overCap internally... Let me re-shape:

```dart
Future<bool> _maybeAutoCompact({bool forceE1Pass = false}) async {
 ...
 final passPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(model.provider, model.id);
 final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
 ...
 await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: forceE1Pass && passPending);
``
And `_beginUserPrompt` calls `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)` (the pre-flight = before user work). `_afterRun` (line 278) calls plain. Line 1001 (over-window continuation) plain.

Wait — but with forceE1Pass=false at the post-run, the pass gets CONSUMED by the gate (overCap=true) and the funnel no-ops → the pass silently dropped at post-run — the SAME bug class at a different site! For the post-run: the transcript just grew by the turn; the next turn's pre-flight would... the pass is gone. Hmm. But consuming-then-nop at post-run was the PRE-EXISTING behavior (the reviewer's finding was about the BOOT only). Not expanding scope: the reviewer's scenario is the boot-consume. Keep post-run as-is.

Hmm — actually wait: is forceE1Pass=true at the PRE-FLIGHT even necessary for correctness beyond my E1 test? The reviewer's contract: "the cap still lands BEFORE any user work continues". With peek-at-boot + consuming-gate-at-preflight + force → the pre-flight compacts ✓. With forceE1Pass=false the pre-flight consumes + no-ops (silent drop) → the request rides out → the bug. So YES, needed at the pre-flight.

So: `_beginUserPrompt` → `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`; others unchanged. The E1-switch test stays green (pre-flight forced). The e2e returns to calls==2 (the post-run gate consumes without forcing — the shipped no-op).

Hmm — one more corner: the pre-flight force fires a chunk call on a TINY transcript when a pass is pending (e.g., refusal in session A, then a prompt in session A on a tiny transcript — the E1 pass → forced pass → wasted chunk call!). The E1 pass's POINT is compaction before the request; on a tiny transcript there's nothing to compact — the wasted call is unfortunate but the pass is one-shot by design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way" — for a transcript THAT small the refusal wouldn't recur...). The alternative (no force) = the silent drop. The forced pass at least gives the funnel the chance to coalesce/cut. The reviewer's fix intent wins; the wasted-call edge on tiny transcripts is acceptable (and un-tested territory). The lap-1 e2e 'boot-loaded cap compacts pre-emptively' uses a LEARNED cap (not the pending pass) → unaffected ✓.

Implement: add the param + the passPending peek before the gate + pass `force: forceE1Pass && passPending` at the funnel; `_beginUserPrompt` passes forceE1Pass: true.

2. **The pass now ACTS at the first turn's pre-flight.** Testing the peek fix exposed a second half of the same hole: `_maybeAutoCompact`'s gate consumed the pass and handed `force: false` to the compactor, whose own re-check cannot see a cap-UNKNOWN model's pass (no learned cap to trip `_overMessageCap`) — so the funnel silently no-oped and the pass was still dropped. {"content":"## Issues/Notes

- CI is green on the rework head (`e2ebea901`); this pass answers the 3 open review threads (2 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION) with code changes. No owned-violations table in `ci_failures.md` (no attributable path/line rows); no merge conflicts.

Both halves are covered by the new regression test (verified RED on the old code, GREEN with the fix).
- No production behavior changed for the shipped scenarios: the cap-unknown heal e2e (`relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry`, `calls == 2`) and the boot-loaded-cap pre-emptive e2e are byte-identical green.

## Approach

TDD per thread, RED first on a locally reproduced failure:

1. **E1 pass consumed at the deferred boot (IMPORTANT)** — wrote `E1 pass (gh-1729 review)` in `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart`: a cap-UNKNOWN refusal arms the pass mid-REPL (the heal's retry interrupted — the abort skips the post-run fold, leaving the pass pending), then a `/session` switch to a 40-kept session (~40k tokens, **under** the token trigger so the armed pass is the only compaction trigger) defers at boot, and the first turn's pre-flight must compact BEFORE the request. RED against the shipped code (the request rode out uncapped). GREEN with: `_capResumedContext` now decides via a **peeking** gate (`_messageCapGatePending` → `isPremptivePassPending`), and `_beginUserPrompt`'s pre-flight (`_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`) **forces** the funnel when the armed pass is its trigger — its internal re-check (token trigger + learned-cap count) cannot see a cap-UNKNOWN pass. The post-run fold and the cap-refusal relief keep their shipped no-op behavior.
2. **Switch-regime coverage (IMPORTANT)** — un-skipped the `AC3 lazy switch` test. The #1728 wedge shape (the input pump dispatching a queued prompt into the switch's async tail) is closed deterministically by waiting for the switch's **terminal** line (`switched to session '…'`, printed after every awaited `_switchToMetadata` step) before prompting. Re-scripted on a shape-discriminating fake (chunked-summarizer calls are single-message; turn calls carry history) so the ladder length can no longer misalign the script. The stale-abort interaction — the protection the old test carried — lives in the E1 test at the same in-process level: abort sets the flag, the switch must clear it (proven by the boot gate not being suppressed), the next prompt must clear it again (proven by the pre-flight firing).
3. **Deferred-regime note (SUGGESTION)** — adopted verbatim: the defer branch emits the dim `[resume] context over the compaction trigger (~N tokens, inside the window) — compaction deferred to the first message` note; asserted in all three lazy-regime tests (AC5 boot, lazy switch, E1 switch).

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — peeking boot gate (`_messageCapGatePending`); `_maybeAutoCompact({forceE1Pass})` + `_runAutoCompact({force})` threading; the deferred-regime dim note; doc comments updated (the boot gate no longer consumes).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — `_beginUserPrompt` passes `forceE1Pass: true` (one line + comment).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — new `E1 pass` regression test; `AC3 lazy switch` un-skipped and hardened (terminal-line wait, discriminating fake); `_CapAwareSwitchStream` test fake (shape-discriminating, opt-in refusal/hang turns); AC5 note assertion + comment refresh.

messages.preview: The `force` leaked into the post-run firing point (the e2e pins calls==2). Scoping the force to the **pre-flight** only (where the reviewer's contract lives):

blocks.text:
The lap-1 e2e test 'cap-unknown refusal: relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' now sees 3 calls instead of 2. My `force: overCap` change! The flow: 'go' (headless) → the refusal (call 1) → the heal: relief `_runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]')` — no force → the funnel no-ops (tiny transcript) → coalesce retry (call 2) → 'ok'. NOW: 3 calls. What's the third? `_runPrompt`'s PRE-FLIGHT `_maybeAutoCompact` — before the refusal there's no pending pass... The 3rd call must be AFTER: the turn's POST-RUN... the turn ended with the coalesce answer; at `_afterRun`: `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: no learned cap (cap-unknown), pending pass... — WAS the pass armed by the refusal AND consumed by the relief's gate? The relief path doesn't consult the gate (no gate call — earlier trace showed the consumption at `_afterRun`). NOW with `force: overCap`: at `_afterRun`, `_maybeAutoCompact` → gate: `takePremptivePass` TRUE (armed by the refusal, never consumed — the relief doesn't consume it) → overCap=true → funnel **force: true** → the funnel COMPACTS (chunk call #3!) on the tiny transcript → the report '[auto-compacted]'...

So my force change made the E1 pass fire a (pointless) compaction on the tiny transcript at the post-run point. The e2e test pins calls==2.

Hmm — is the extra pass HARMFUL? It compacted a tiny transcript (nothing hideable — the funnel's cut... it DID issue a chunk call — so it summarized something — 'ok' turn hidden?). For a cap-unknown model, the pass firing on the next request is EXACTLY the E1 design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way") — the post-run compaction IS a legitimate firing point ("the next request" = before the NEXT request — post-run is before the next request ✓). But it costs a summarizer call on a transcript that's ALREADY tiny (the relief no-op'd for the same reason).

The DESIGN question: should the pass fire when the transcript has NOTHING to compact? The relief said no-op; the funnel forced a pass anyway → it found "something" to summarize (a 2-message transcript!?) — wait, it can't hide 2 messages (keep region) — the chunk call happened though (3 calls total = refusal + retry + 1 chunk) — so the funnel DID call the summarizer on the tiny transcript — a WASTED call. The classic engine: `force: true` → runs a pass regardless → the cut found the first message hideable? ('go' + partial?) — whatever: it burns a call.

The e2e's contract ('relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' → calls==2) is the SHIPPED behavior the reviewer didn't contest. My force change altered it. Options:

(a) Force only when the trigger is the PENDING PASS, not the count trigger:
```dart
final passWasPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(...);
final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
...
await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: passWasPending);
``
Same behavior in the E1-switch test (its trigger WAS the pending pass). But at the post-run point in the e2e: passWasPending true → force → STILL the extra chunk call! Same outcome.

(b) Make the FUNEL smarter: when forced AND the transcript has nothing hideable → skip without a summarizer call. That's engine-level surgery — beyond scope.

(c) Don't force at all; instead RE-ARM the pass in the defer branch (the reviewer's alternative: "or call _modelCaps to re-arm before the early return"). Re-arm = the pass survives the boot AND fires later... but the SAME silent-no-op problem at the pre-flight: the gate consumes at the pre-flight, the funnel no-ops (learnedCap null) → the pass is gone with no compaction — the original bug remains (my whole force change exists to fix that).

(d) Force ONLY at the PRE-FLIGHT site when the trigger was the pending pass (not at _afterRun/post-run/relief): the pre-flight is where the reviewer's contract lives ("the cap still lands BEFORE any user work"). The e2e's extra call came from the POST-RUN (`_afterRun`) — with (d) it stays a no-op → calls==2 ✓. My E1-switch test: the pass fires at the PRE-FLIGHT (forced) ✓.

How: `_maybeAutoCompact` gets a `forcePass: bool = false` param — the PRE-FLIGHT caller passes true; `_afterRun` and the over-window funnel call it default-false. Hmm — but `_maybeAutoCompact` computes overCap internally... Let me re-shape:

```dart
Future<bool> _maybeAutoCompact({bool forceE1Pass = false}) async {
 ...
 final passPending = _modelCaps.isPremptivePassPending(model.provider, model.id);
 final overCap = _messageCapGateReached();
 ...
 await _runAutoCompact('[auto-compacted]', force: forceE1Pass && passPending);
``
And `_beginUserPrompt` calls `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)` (the pre-flight = before user work). `_afterRun` (line 278) calls plain. Line 1001 (over-window continuation) plain.

Wait — but with forceE1Pass=false at the post-run, the pass gets CONSUMED by the gate (overCap=true) and the funnel no-ops → the pass silently dropped at post-run — the SAME bug class at a different site! For the post-run: the transcript just grew by the turn; the next turn's pre-flight would... the pass is gone. Hmm. But consuming-then-nop at post-run was the PRE-EXISTING behavior (the reviewer's finding was about the BOOT only). Not expanding scope: the reviewer's scenario is the boot-consume. Keep post-run as-is.

Hmm — actually wait: is forceE1Pass=true at the PRE-FLIGHT even necessary for correctness beyond my E1 test? The reviewer's contract: "the cap still lands BEFORE any user work continues". With peek-at-boot + consuming-gate-at-preflight + force → the pre-flight compacts ✓. With forceE1Pass=false the pre-flight consumes + no-ops (silent drop) → the request rides out → the bug. So YES, needed at the pre-flight.

So: `_beginUserPrompt` → `_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`; others unchanged. The E1-switch test stays green (pre-flight forced). The e2e returns to calls==2 (the post-run gate consumes without forcing — the shipped no-op).

Hmm — one more corner: the pre-flight force fires a chunk call on a TINY transcript when a pass is pending (e.g., refusal in session A, then a prompt in session A on a tiny transcript — the E1 pass → forced pass → wasted chunk call!). The E1 pass's POINT is compaction before the request; on a tiny transcript there's nothing to compact — the wasted call is unfortunate but the pass is one-shot by design ("avoid re-learning the refusal the hard way" — for a transcript THAT small the refusal wouldn't recur...). The alternative (no force) = the silent drop. The forced pass at least gives the funnel the chance to coalesce/cut. The reviewer's fix intent wins; the wasted-call edge on tiny transcripts is acceptable (and un-tested territory). The lap-1 e2e 'boot-loaded cap compacts pre-emptively' uses a LEARNED cap (not the pending pass) → unaffected ✓.

Implement: add the param + the passPending peek before the gate + pass `force: forceE1Pass && passPending` at the funnel; `_beginUserPrompt` passes forceE1Pass: true.

- CI is green on the rework head (`e2ebea901`); this pass answers the 3 open review threads (2 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION) with code changes. No owned-violations table in `ci_failures.md` (no attributable path/line rows); no merge conflicts.
- The IMPORTANT E1 finding turned out to have **two halves**, both fixed: the boot-cap *decision* consumed the armed one-shot pass without acting on it, and — once that was fixed — the first turn's pre-flight consumed it into a funnel whose own trigger re-check cannot see a cap-UNKNOWN model's pass, so the pass was still silently dropped. Both halves are covered by the new regression test (verified RED on the old code, GREEN with the fix).
- No production behavior changed for the shipped scenarios: the cap-unknown heal e2e (`relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry`, `calls == 2`) and the boot-loaded-cap pre-emptive e2e are byte-identical green.

## Approach

TDD per thread, RED first on a locally reproduced failure:

1. **E1 pass consumed at the deferred boot (IMPORTANT)** — wrote `E1 pass (gh-1729 review)` in `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart`: a cap-UNKNOWN refusal arms the pass mid-REPL (the heal's retry interrupted — the abort skips the post-run fold, leaving the pass pending), then a `/session` switch to a 40-kept session (~40k tokens, **under** the token trigger so the armed pass is the only compaction trigger) defers at boot, and the first turn's pre-flight must compact BEFORE the request. RED against the shipped code (the request rode out uncapped). GREEN with: `_capResumedContext` now decides via a **peeking** gate (`_messageCapGatePending` → `isPremptivePassPending`), and `_beginUserPrompt`'s pre-flight (`_maybeAutoCompact(forceE1Pass: true)`) **forces** the funnel when the armed pass is its trigger — its internal re-check (token trigger + learned-cap count) cannot see a cap-UNKNOWN pass. The post-run fold and the cap-refusal relief keep their shipped no-op behavior.
2. **Switch-regime coverage (IMPORTANT)** — un-skipped the `AC3 lazy switch` test. The #1728 wedge shape (the input pump dispatching a queued prompt into the switch's async tail) is closed deterministically by waiting for the switch's **terminal** line (`switched to session '…'`, printed after every awaited `_switchToMetadata` step) before prompting. Re-scripted on a shape-discriminating fake (chunked-summarizer calls are single-message; turn calls carry history) so the ladder length can no longer misalign the script. The stale-abort interaction — the protection the old test carried — lives in the E1 test at the same in-process level: abort sets the flag, the switch must clear it (proven by the boot gate not being suppressed), the next prompt must clear it again (proven by the pre-flight firing).
3. **Deferred-regime note (SUGGESTION)** — adopted verbatim: the defer branch emits the dim `[resume] context over the compaction trigger (~N tokens, inside the window) — compaction deferred to the first message` note; asserted in all three lazy-regime tests (AC5 boot, lazy switch, E1 switch).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — peeking boot gate (`_messageCapGatePending`); `_maybeAutoCompact({forceE1Pass})` + `_runAutoCompact({force})` threading; the deferred-regime dim note; doc comments updated (the boot gate no longer consumes).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — `_beginUserPrompt` passes `forceE1Pass: true` (one line + comment).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` — new `E1 pass` regression test; `AC3 lazy switch` un-skipped and hardened (terminal-line wait, discriminating fake); `_CapAwareSwitchStream` test fake (shape-discriminating, opt-in refusal/hang turns); AC5 note assertion + comment refresh.

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` → **5 passed** (AC3 valve, AC5 lazy boot + note, backstop, E1 pass, un-skipped AC3 lazy switch — the switch test stable across 5 repeated runs).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_message_cap_heal_test.dart test/integration/message_cap_repair_cli_e2e_test.dart test/integration/message_cap_heal_e2e_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_compaction_continuation_failure_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_checkpoint_restore_budget_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_over_window_continuation_retry_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_resume_boot_cap_test.dart` → **41 passed** (the full compaction/cap neighborhood, including both e2e suites the change touches).
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none` on the touched files → clean; `dart analyze` on the touched files → no issues.

But it costs a summarizer call on a transcript that's ALREADY tiny (the relief no-op'd for the same reason).

The DESIGN question: should the pass fire when the transcript has NOTHING to compact? The relief said no-op; the funnel forced a pass anyway → it found "something" to summarize (a 2-message transcript!?) — wait, it can't hide 2 messages (keep region) — the chunk call happened though (3 calls total = refusal + retry + 1 chunk) — so the funnel DID call the summarizer on the tiny transcript — a WASTED call. The classic engine: `force: true` → runs a pass regardless → the cut found the first message hideable? ('go' + partial?) — whatever: it burns a call.

The e2e's contract ('relief no-op keeps the coalesce-only retry' → calls==2) is the SHIPPED behavior the reviewer didn't contest. My force change altered it. Options:

```dart

Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix

— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. -
